learning.title: claudeConfigDirectory deletes every other attempt directory, so a new worker mode needs its own config directory
learning.trigger: Adding a worker mode that runs the Claude CLI (a reviewer, a second harness action) in the same worker state directory as the Claude harness.
learning.mistake: `claudeConfigDirectory` first removes every entry of `<stateDir>/claude-harness` except `sessions`, then makes `claude-harness/<attemptId>`. It assumes it is the only user of that directory. A second mode that calls it deletes another running attempt's config and isolated HOME, and the failure shows up in the other attempt as a vanished credential copy or a missing session file.
learning.rule: Give each worker mode its own attempt root and config directory under its own state subdirectory (the reviewer uses `<stateDir>/reviews`), built from the shared `prepareHarnessHome`, and never call `claudeConfigDirectory` from a mode that can run beside another Claude attempt. Sweep only your own subdirectory at startup, never a sibling.

verification.requirement: Every reviewer case leaves no attempt root under `reviews`, no extra worktree record and an untouched operator repository.

learning.boundary: The coordinator and the harness still share `claudeConfigDirectory`; they rely on never running at the same time on one worker. This learning does not change that.
